newsitem.title: UK: Mowlem back in profit, confirms unit float.
newsitem.headline: Mowlem back in profit, confirms unit float.

text.p: John Mowlem and Co Plc, the building to management services group, returned to profit in 1996 and said that prospects for further growth this year are encouraging.
The company made pretax profit of 16.7 million stg in 1996 compared with a loss of 30.0 million in 1995, but turnover decreased to 1.41 billion from 1.46 billion previously.
"The whole group has made progress in 1996. We see the prospects for continuing profitable growth as encouraging," said chief executive John Gains.
The company added that further growth would be primarily driven by management actions rather than an increase in market buoyancy.
The group also confirmed it plans the partial flotation of its access products and services division later this year.
"Opportunities for further growth will be presented for both Mowlem and SGB by the partial flotation of the access division," said Gains.
Mowlem said that its sustained focus on margins is likely to generate earnings growth in its construction services.
